prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
answers:
[goal] One regex in `./regex.txt` that, via `re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE)`, returns the last valid `YYYY-MM-DD` on every line containing a valid IPv4 address, nothing for address-free lines.

[action] Wrote the regex (single capture group around the date, so `findall` returns dates only), plus a scratch test at `tmp/test_regex.py`:

```
^(?=.*(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])(?![0-9A-Za-z])).*(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9])))(?![0-9A-Za-z])
```

How it works: `^` + lookahead requires a well-formed address somewhere on the line; the greedy `.*` then backtracks to the rightmost valid date, so the capture is the last one. `.` never crosses a newline, so lines stay independent and results come in file order.

Assumptions for what the brief left open:
- Adjacency test is `[0-9A-Za-z]` on both sides of both date and address, exactly as worded; punctuation/hyphen/dot adjacency is allowed (so `1.2.3.4:8080`, `(2026-05-05)`, and `2026-05-05-06` all count).
- Year is any 4 digits; no leap-year rule, so Feb 01-29 is valid every year; 30-day months reject day 31; month 00 and day 00 invalid.
- Leading-zero octets are rejected structurally: `01.2.3.4` and `1.02.3.4` match nothing.
- A line with an address but no valid date yields nothing; a line with a date but no address yields nothing.

[result] On `./server.log`:

```
['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05', '2026-04-02']
```

Lines 2 and 4 (no address, incl. the decoy `job 7781-20-4410`) give nothing; lines 1, 3, 5 give their last date (`2026-04-01`, `2026-04-05`, `2026-04-02`). Same result with CRLF line endings. 25 edge cases pass, `failures 0`: `255.255.255.255` and `0.0.0.0` accepted, `256.1.1.1` rejected, `x1.1.1.1` / `1.1.1.1x` rejected, `2026-02-29` accepted, `2026-02-30` / `2026-04-31` / `2026-06-31` / `2026-11-31` / `2026-01-00` / `2026-00-10` rejected, `12026-05-05` / `2026-05-05x` / `x2026-05-05` rejected, rightmost-date selection on multi-date lines, and fallback to the previous valid date when the last token is invalid. Group count asserted as 1.

Known by running the exact call signature the brief specifies (`re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE)` with the file read and stripped) and reading the raw output above, not by reasoning about the pattern. No browser or app was opened; only files in the workspace were touched.
